learning_outcomes.text: Explain and apply the relationships among position, velocity, and acceleration in particle kinematics using Cartesian, normal-tangential, and polar coordinate systems.
Formulate and solve equations of motion for particles using Newton’s laws and free-body diagrams.
Apply work-energy and impulse-momentum methods to particle motion, and interpret conservation laws of energy and momentum.
Analyze translation, rotation, and general planar motion in rigid-body kinematics, including angular velocity, angular acceleration, and relative motion concepts.
Formulate mass moment of inertia, force-moment equations, and planar equations of motion in rigid-body dynamics.
Theoretically model and analyze the dynamic behavior of mechanical systems, interpret the results, and apply them to engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Basic Concepts : Space, Time, Mass, Force, Particle, Rijid Body, Coordinate Systems, Gravitation
Kinematics of Particle (position, velocity, acceleration) in Rectangular and Polar Coordinate Systems

Normal and Tangential Coordinates (position, velocity, acceleration), Rectilinear Motion, Plane Curvilinear Motion, Space Curvilinear MotionNormal and Tangential Coordinates (position, velocity, acceleration), Rectilinear Motion, Plane Curvilinear Motion
Relative Motion (Translating Axes) (in Non-rotating Coordinate System)
Relative Motion (Translating Axes) (in Rotating Coordinate System)
Kinetics of Particle : Equation of Motion and Solution of Problems in different Coordinate Systems.
Work and Kinetic Energy - Concervation of Energy
Impulse and Momentum, Conservation of Momentum
Linear Impulse and Linear momentum, Angular Impulse and Angular Momentum
Particle Systems, Energy of Particle Systems, Momentum of Particle Systems, Impulse-Momentum Relations
